title: Spell-IT-Out
description: Spell-IT-Out is an EEG dataset of 25 native Italian speakers who listened to sentences, repeated them, and then produced them syllable by syllable at a fixed pace, either aloud (overt) or silently (covert). Each participant completed 3 overt and 3 covert runs of 20 trials. Recordings used 61 EEG channels plus 1 EOG channel at 2048 Hz. Hand-corrected word and syllable timings of overt speech are provided as events, and derivatives include preprocessed continuous EEG and syllable epochs for machine learning.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 64-channel ANT Neuro waveguard cap and eego sports amplifier at 2048 Hz (reference CPz, ground AFz, impedances below 10 kΩ), with an EOG electrode below the left eye. Data were acquired with ROS-Neuro in an electrically shielded, acoustically isolated room. Overt speech was recorded by microphone and segmented with Silero-VAD. It was aligned with the Montreal Forced Aligner and corrected manually in Praat at sentence, word and syllable level.
